mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is a carboxylic acid?
mcqs.explanation: Carboxylic acids contain the –COOH functional group. CH3COOH (acetic acid) has this group, whereas the other options are an alcohol, an aldehyde, and an alkane respectively.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate functional groups to compound properties
mcqs.question: How does the presence of a hydroxyl (‑OH) group affect the boiling point of a compound compared to a hydrocarbon of similar molecular weight?

options.D: It makes the compound gaseous at room temperature

mcqs.explanation: The –OH group can form hydrogen bonds between molecules, which requires more energy to break, thus raising the boiling point relative to non‑polar hydrocarbons of comparable size.

mcqs.question: The functional group –CHO is characteristic of which class of organic compounds?
mcqs.explanation: The –CHO group (a carbonyl attached to a hydrogen) defines aldehydes. Alcohols have –OH, ketones have –CO– (carbonyl between two carbons), and carboxylic acids have –COOH.

mcqs.question: Which of the following compounds is an alcohol?
mcqs.explanation: Alcohols contain the –OH functional group. CH3CH2OH (ethanol) has this group, while the others are a carboxylic acid, an aldehyde, and an alkane.

mcqs.question: Which compound below is an aldehyde?
mcqs.explanation: CH3CHO contains the –CHO group, the defining feature of aldehydes. Option A is an alcohol, C is a ketone, and D is a carboxylic acid.

mcqs.question: A compound with formula C4H8O has a carbonyl group attached to two carbon atoms. Which class does it belong to?
mcqs.explanation: When the carbonyl (C=O) is bonded to two carbon atoms, the compound is a ketone. Aldehydes have the carbonyl at the end of the chain (bonded to hydrogen), alcohols have –OH, and carboxylic acids have –COOH.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes a carboxylic acid?

options.A: It contains a –COOH group where a carbonyl and a hydroxyl are attached to the same carbon.
options.C: It is the same as an aldehyde.
options.D: It contains only a carbonyl group without any hydroxyl.

mcqs.answer: It contains a –COOH group where a carbonyl and a hydroxyl are attached to the same carbon.
mcqs.explanation: Carboxylic acids are defined by the –COOH functional group (a carbonyl C=O and a hydroxyl –OH on the same carbon). The other options describe aldehydes or omit the hydroxyl part, which is a common misconception.

mcqs.learning_point: Relate functional groups to compound properties
mcqs.question: Why do carboxylic acids generally have higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular weight?

options.A: Each carboxylic acid molecule can form two hydrogen bonds with neighboring molecules.
options.B: Carboxylic acids are non‑polar, leading to stronger van der Waals forces.
options.C: They have a lower molecular weight than alcohols.
options.D: Carboxylic acids cannot hydrogen‑bond, so they evaporate more slowly.

mcqs.answer: Each carboxylic acid molecule can form two hydrogen bonds with neighboring molecules.
mcqs.explanation: The –COOH group can both donate and accept hydrogen bonds, allowing each molecule to engage in two hydrogen‑bond interactions, which raises the boiling point. Alcohols can form only one hydrogen bond per –OH group. Options B, C, and D are incorrect statements.
